body_text: Two pool drain cover products sold through Amazon have been recalled after federal safety officials determined that they may fail to provide proper protection against dangerous underwater suction hazards. The recalled products, sold under the names Sviyatp and OeyUoc, were manufactured in China and distributed as replacement drain covers for residential swimming pools. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) announced the recalls on July 23, 2026, after finding that both products did not comply with federal safety requirements designed to prevent swimmer entrapment. The affected covers were sold online through Amazon.com between March and June 2026, with each product priced at approximately $18. Although no injuries or accidents have been reported in connection with either product, safety officials are urging pool owners to immediately stop using pools equipped with these drain covers until the recalled parts are removed. Recalled Pool Drain Covers Did Not Meet Federal Safety Standards The recalled products failed to meet the requirements established under the Virginia Graeme Baker Pool and Spa Safety Act, a federal law created to reduce the risk of swimmers becoming trapped by powerful suction forces from pool and spa drains. Pool drain covers play a critical role in preventing accidents because they are designed to distribute suction pressure and stop body parts, hair, or clothing from becoming trapped against a drain opening. If a drain cover is poorly designed or does not meet required standards, it may increase the risk of serious injury or drowning. According to the CPSC, approximately 670 Sviyatp pool drain covers and around 404 OeyUoc drain covers were sold to consumers. Both products were marketed as replacement drain covers for home swimming pools. The Sviyatp drain cover was sold by Shenzhen Meilanxiang Trading Co., Ltd., operating under the Sviyatp name. The OeyUoc product was sold by Shenzhen Yuanxinxiang Trade Co., Ltd., operating as Yuanxinxiang. Both companies are based in China, and the recalled products were manufactured there. How Consumers Can Identify the Recalled Products One of the challenges with this recall is that neither drain cover has identifying information printed directly on the product itself. This means consumers may have difficulty determining whether they own one of the recalled covers after installation. The CPSC advises customers to check the original packaging if it is still available. The Sviyatp product packaging includes the following identifying information: Product codes: X0050114ZZ and SV-SP1030-001 Product description: “Sviyatp Dual Suction Outlet” Manufacturing label: “Made in China” The OeyUoc product packaging includes: Product codes: X00501CQ7P and OY-WG1048E-1P Product description: “OeyUoc WG1048…Skimmer Lid SP1030” Manufacturing label: “Made in China” Both recalled products were shipped with two stainless steel screws. What Pool Owners Should Do Now Consumers who believe they may have one of these drain covers installed should stop using the pool immediately until the product is removed. The CPSC recommends that owners take the following steps: Remove the recalled drain cover from the pool. Mark the product with the word “RECALL” using permanent marker. Take a photograph of the removed cover. If possible, cut or damage the outer structure of the cover so it cannot be installed again. Contact the appropriate company to request a full refund. Owners of Sviyatp drain covers should send identification photographs to SviyatpRecall@qq.com . Owners of OeyUoc drain covers should send photographs to OeyUocChina@163.com . Consumers should avoid reinstalling the products or giving them to another person, as doing so could create a safety risk. Why Pool Drain Safety Rules Matter The safety requirements involved in this recall are connected to the Virginia Graeme Baker Pool and Spa Safety Act, which was created following a tragic accident involving a young child. The law was named after Virginia Graeme Baker, a 7-year-old girl who died in 2002 after becoming trapped by the suction of a hot tub drain. Following her daughter’s death, her mother, Nancy Baker, worked with safety organizations and lawmakers to push for stronger protections in swimming pools and spas. The legislation was signed into law in December 2007 and became effective in 2008. It established national safety requirements for drain covers and other anti-entrapment measures, particularly in public pools and spas. While the law primarily focuses on public aquatic facilities, its safety principles are also important for residential pool owners. Properly designed and installed drain covers can help reduce the risk of dangerous suction-related accidents. Online Marketplace Safety Concerns The recall also highlights growing concerns about safety standards for products sold through online marketplaces. Consumers often purchase replacement pool parts, accessories, and maintenance equipment online because of convenience and lower prices. However, product safety information can sometimes be difficult to verify, especially when items are imported from overseas manufacturers. Experts recommend that pool owners purchase replacement parts from trusted suppliers, verify that products meet recognized safety standards, and keep product packaging or receipts for future reference. Pool equipment should not be treated as a simple household accessory. Components such as drain covers, filters, ladders, and safety barriers can directly affect swimmer protection. Final Reminder for Pool Owners The recall of the Sviyatp and OeyUoc pool drain covers serves as an important reminder that even small replacement parts can have major safety consequences. Consumers who have installed either recalled product should stop using the pool, remove the cover, and contact the manufacturer for refund instructions. Regular inspection of pool equipment and awareness of safety recalls can help prevent accidents and protect swimmers, especially children. Pool owners are encouraged to stay informed through official safety agencies and check whether their equipment meets current safety requirements before allowing anyone to swim. Sources Information in this article is based on details released by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission regarding the recall of Sviyatp and OeyUoc pool drain covers, along with public safety information related to the Virginia Graeme Baker Pool and Spa Safety Act. Disclaimer This article is provided for informational purposes only and does not replace official recall notices, manufacturer instructions, or professional safety advice. Consumers should verify recall information directly with official agencies or product manufacturers before taking action.

title: WhatsApp Business API Limitations Every Shopify Merchant Should Know
summary: Zoko is an all-in-one system that leverages the WhatsApp API to help you do business, on WhatsApp. Go beyond chatting - reach customers, enable product discovery, collect payments, get feedback - all on WhatsApp.
body_text: You set up an abandoned cart recovery message on WhatsApp, sent it, and heard nothing back. No delivery confirmation or customer response. If your first thought was “technical error,” you were not entirely wrong. The real issue is often a rule nobody flagged before you went live. The WhatsApp Business API does not work like email or SMS. It runs on defined limits: a 24-hour customer service window, approved message templates for re-engagement, Meta-set messaging limits, setup rules for phone numbers, and extra eligibility requirements for features like calling and groups. For Shopify merchants, these limits affect cart recovery, COD confirmation, shipping updates, support speed, broadcasts, and customer engagement on WhatsApp. Knowing these WhatsApp Business API limitations up front helps you design better workflows rather than fixing broken ones after launch. ‍ Key Takeaways WhatsApp Business API limitations directly affect Shopify workflows such as cart recovery, COD confirmation, shipping updates, support replies, and broadcasts. The 24-hour customer service window controls when merchants can send free-form replies; after that, approved templates are needed. Messaging limits and account quality shape how many customers a store can reach through WhatsApp campaigns. Group messaging and voice calling have specific access rules, so most Shopify stores should build around one-to-one customer journeys first. Zoko helps merchants manage these limits through WhatsApp sales, support, COD, catalogue, broadcast, and automation workflows. ‍ WhatsApp Business API vs. the WhatsApp Business App If you are running a Shopify store on WhatsApp at any meaningful volume, you are likely better served by the API, not only the App. The WhatsApp Business App is the free, phone-based tool built for small businesses handling conversations manually. The API connects WhatsApp to platforms, CRMs, automation tools, and Shopify workflows through providers like Zoko. That makes it more suitable for multi-agent support, broadcasts, chatbot automation, order updates, catalogue selling, and COD workflows. ‍ WhatsApp Business API vs WhatsApp Business App Feature WhatsApp Business API WhatsApp Business App Broadcast Scale Governed by Meta messaging limits and opt-in rules Up to 256 contacts per broadcast list Multi-Agent Access Supported through platforms like Zoko Limited to app and linked-device use Chatbot/Automation Supports workflow automation and AI agents Limited to basic app tools Broadcast Reach Opted-in customers, without needing them to save your number Recipients must have your number saved Shopify Integration Supported through Zoko Not built for Shopify automation Also Read: WhatsApp Business API Features and Setup Guide ‍ 6 Main WhatsApp Business API Limitations at a Glance WhatsApp Business API Limitations Limitation What It Means in Practice 24-hour customer service window After a customer messages you, you have 24 hours to reply freely. After that, use approved templates. Template approval for re-engagement Business-initiated messages outside the service window need Meta-approved templates. Messaging limits Meta controls how many unique customers you can reach with template messages. Group messaging has specific eligibility rules Group API access exists, but it is not the default model for Shopify support or sales workflows. Calling requires specific setup WhatsApp Business Calling API is available, but it requires Cloud API setup and eligibility. Phone numbers have setup rules Your number must be registered correctly before it can send and receive API messages. ‍ Limitation 1: You Can Only Message Freely Within a 24-Hour Session ‍ Once a customer messages your store, a 24-hour customer service window opens. During that window, your team can send regular service replies through the WhatsApp Business API. After it closes, you need an approved template to restart the conversation, as explained in Meta’s service message documentation . ‍ How the Session Works During the 24-hour period, you can reply with product images, payment links, order details, voice notes, or support answers. Once the window closes, free-form replies stop working. Any follow-up must use an approved message template. For example, a customer messages at 10 AM Monday asking about a product. If your team replies at 11 AM Tuesday, the customer service window has already closed. That reply needs to be sent as an approved template, not a regular message. ‍ What It Means for Cart Recovery and Order Follow-ups For Shopify merchants, this rule directly affects abandoned cart recovery, COD confirmation, payment reminders, and order follow-ups. Even a short nudge like "Still interested?" needs Meta's clearance after 24 hours have passed. Also Read: Step-by-Step Guide to Recovering Abandoned Carts on WhatsApp ‍ Limitation 2: Business-Initiated Messages Need Meta-Approved Templates If your store starts or restarts a conversation outside the customer service window, you need an approved message template. This applies to common Shopify workflows like abandoned cart reminders, COD confirmation, shipping alerts, reorder prompts, and review requests. ‍ What a Template Message Is A template is a reusable message format submitted for approval before use. Meta explains template rules in its official WhatsApp message template documentation . Common ecommerce template use cases include: COD order confirmation requests Shipping and delivery updates Abandoned cart reminders Reorder reminders Post-delivery review requests Payment or prepaid conversion prompts For Shopify teams, templates should be prepared before a campaign or automation goes live. Otherwise, a workflow may be ready in your tool but blocked at the message level. ‍ Why Templates Get Rejected Rejection is one of the most common friction points for merchants new to the API. Most rejections follow a recognisable pattern. Common causes include: Unclear purpose: The message does not explain why the customer is receiving it. Weak opt-in context: The message feels unexpected or irrelevant to the customer. Incorrect variables: Dynamic fields need to follow Meta’s required formatting. Policy issues: The message conflicts with the WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy or Meta’s Commerce Policy . A good template should have one clear purpose, a relevant customer context, and a simple action. For example, a COD confirmation template should focus on confirming the order, not adding unrelated promotions. ‍ Limitation 3: Your Account Has Messaging Limits Meta assigns a daily cap on unique customers you can reach with business-initiated messages. It starts low and moves based on your account behavior. ‍ How the Tier System Works ‍ According to Meta's official Messaging Limits documentation , all accounts begin at a set daily threshold and progress through tiers as trust is established: WhatsApp Business Messaging Limits Level Messaging Limit Starting limit for newly created business portfolios 250 Scaled limit 2,000 Scaled limit 10,000 Scaled limit 100,000 Highest limit Unlimited As of October 2025, these caps apply per business portfolio rather than per phone number. Adding a second WhatsApp number does not increase your cap. Both numbers share the same tier. For Shopify merchants running more than one store under the same portfolio, this directly affects campaign planning. ‍ What Moves You Up or Down a Tier Meta upgrades your tier automatically when you consistently use a meaningful portion of your current daily cap while holding a Green quality rating. Quality is shaped by what recipients do after receiving your messages: block rates, spam reports, and overall relevance all factor in. Keeping your block rate below 1% is healthy. Above 2% puts your quality rating at risk. Note: As of October 2025 , a quality rating drop no longer triggers an automatic tier downgrade. A Red rating prevents you from advancing to a higher tier, but your current cap stays in place. Also Read: How to Send WhatsApp Broadcast Messages at Scale ‍ Limitation 4: Group Messaging Is Not the Default Workflow for Shopify Automation The old assumption was simple: WhatsApp Business API conversations are one-to-one. That is still the most practical model for Shopify sales, support, cart recovery, COD confirmation, and order updates. However, it is no longer accurate to say group messaging has “no workaround.” Meta now documents a WhatsApp Groups API , with access rules tied to business eligibility. For most Shopify merchants, the better takeaway is this: do not design core WhatsApp commerce workflows around groups. Abandoned cart messages, order tracking, payment links, support answers, and product recommendations need customer-specific data. They work best as one-to-one journeys connected to Shopify. Groups may support specific community or announcement use cases, but they should not replace personalised customer messaging. ‍ Limitation 5: Voice Calls Are Available but Require Setup Meta introduced the WhatsApp Business Calling API so businesses can add voice calling to customer journeys. The feature can help with high-intent sales, delivery issues, COD verification, and support escalations. Access is not automatic for every new API account. Meta’s Cloud API Calling documentation includes specific setup and eligibility requirements. Most Shopify merchants should launch with strong messaging workflows first: Abandoned checkout recovery COD confirmation Order and shipping notifications Product questions Support replies Review requests Calling can be added later when your account, support volume, and customer journey justify it. ‍ Limitation 6: Your Phone Number Has Registration Constraints A WhatsApp business phone number must be registered before it can send and receive messages through Cloud API. Meta’s business phone number documentation explains the registration requirement. Historically, using the same number across the WhatsApp Business App and API was difficult. Meta now supports onboarding some WhatsApp Business App users to Cloud API through an official flow, explained in its Business App user onboarding documentation . For Shopify merchants, the practical issue is customer continuity. If buyers already know your WhatsApp number, changing it can create friction. Zoko helps merchants connect Shopify with WhatsApp and set up the right number, workflows, templates, and automations without treating the API as a manual technical project. Connect Your Shopify Store to WhatsApp . ‍ What These Limitations Mean for Your Shopify Store Each limit affects a different part of daily ecommerce operations. Here is where Shopify merchants will feel them most. ‍ Customer Support Response Time Becomes a Business Requirement If your team misses the 24-hour customer service window, a normal support reply may need to become a template message. That slows down conversations and can hurt conversion when the customer is still deciding. For busy Shopify stores, this makes response speed more than a support metric. It affects cart recovery, product questions, payment clarifications, and order-related conversations. ‍ Broadcast Campaigns Need a Different Workflow Than Email You cannot treat WhatsApp like an email newsletter. WhatsApp broadcasts need opt-in, approved templates when required, and tighter audience selection. This is good discipline. A back-in-stock alert to interested shoppers is stronger than a generic discount blast to everyone. Relevance protects quality and improves the chance that customers reply, buy, or reorder. ‍ COD Confirmations and Order Flows Depend on Approved Templates COD confirmations, shipping alerts, and reorder reminders are business-critical for many Shopify stores, especially in India and other WhatsApp-first markets. If these templates are not ready before launch, teams end up confirming orders manually, chasing customers after the service window closes, or sending delayed updates. The better approach is to prepare these workflows before campaigns and order flows go live. ‍ How Zoko Helps Shopify Merchants Work Within These Limits ‍ Zoko is built around WhatsApp Business API rules, so merchants do not have to manage every constraint manually. ‍ Flows Timed to the Session Window Zoko Flows helps merchants automate key ecommerce journeys at the right moment. Abandoned checkout recovery, COD confirmation, shipping updates, reorder reminders, and review collection can run without constant manual follow-up. ‍ Template and Broadcast Management in One Place Through Zoko’s Broadcasts , merchants can send campaigns to relevant customer segments instead of treating every subscriber the same. This helps protect account quality and keeps broadcasts tied to real shopper intent. ‍ AI Agents That Keep Conversations Moving Zoko’s AI agents , including Guru, Wismo, and Sello, help answer common questions, resolve order-tracking queries, and support sales conversations inside WhatsApp. This keeps customer interactions moving before interest drops or the service window closes. ‍ Shopify Catalogue and WhatsApp Commerce Zoko also helps merchants sync their Shopify catalogue with WhatsApp, so customers can browse and buy inside the chat. That matters because the API is not only a support channel. For Shopify stores, it can become a direct sales channel connected to product discovery, payments, follow-ups, and retention. Also Read: How to Create a WhatsApp AI Chatbot for Real-Time Interaction ‍ Wrapping Up WhatsApp Business API limitations are not dealbreakers for Shopify merchants. They are operating rules that affect when you can reply, which messages need approval, how broadcasts should be planned, and how customer conversations move through WhatsApp. The stores that get this right prepare templates before launch, respond before the 24-hour customer service window closes, send broadcasts to relevant segments, and keep COD, shipping, cart recovery, and support flows ready as they scale. Zoko helps Shopify merchants turn those rules into practical sales, support, COD, catalogue, and automation workflows. Start your 7-day free trial to set up WhatsApp for your Shopify store, or book a demo to walk through the right setup with the Zoko team. ‍ Frequently Asked Questions ‍ Q. What are the main WhatsApp Business API limitations? The main WhatsApp Business API limitations include the 24-hour customer service window, approved templates for re-engagement, Meta-set messaging limits, business phone-number setup rules, and extra eligibility requirements for features like calling and groups. ‍ Q. Can I send promotional messages on the WhatsApp Business API at any time? No. Outside an active customer service window, promotional or marketing outreach must use approved templates and follow WhatsApp’s messaging policies. ‍ Q. What happens if I hit my messaging limit? Messages beyond your current limit may not be sent until capacity becomes available again. Check your current limit in WhatsApp Manager and plan broadcasts around priority segments. ‍ Q. Can multiple agents use the same WhatsApp number? Yes. Through a platform like Zoko, multiple team members can manage customer conversations from one WhatsApp number. ‍ Q. Does adding a second phone number increase my daily limit? Not automatically. Messaging capacity is governed by Meta’s WhatsApp Business Platform rules, so adding numbers should be done for operational reasons, not as a shortcut around quality or sending limits.
